reason: The word is used for different objects, and the sourced statistical meanings are already pages or rest on a single entry. The existing loss-and-risk page is expected loss of a decision. Dodge printed pp. 461–462 instead defines epidemiological risk, the probability a disease appears in a population during a time interval, so Risk is not an alias of loss-and-risk. ESL §2.4 pp. 18–20 defines expected prediction error under a loss and does not use the word risk for the epidemiological probability. ISL discusses test error. The NIST glossary has no risk entry. OpenIntro chapter 1 uses risk in ordinary clinical language, not as a defined incidence probability.
